speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance. To help me understand your condition, how long have these symptoms been present, and did they start suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) secondary to recent upper respiratory infection.

I suspect your recent garlic consumption isn't the primary cause of the spinning sensation, as BPPV is common after viral infections affecting the inner ear. I would like to confirm if your dizziness is triggered specifically by changes in head position, such as looking up or rolling over in bed, and if you have experienced any hearing loss or ringing in your ears.
